arguments.summary: A critical credential compromise incident was detected originating from external IP 185.220.101.42. The threat actor conducted reconnaissance via port scanning against an internal IT asset (WS-IT-101 at 10.0.2.15), successfully authenticated using compromised credentials (CORP\helpdesk), and subsequently performed a pass-the-hash attack to compromise all 23 user accounts within the Finance OU. Despite detection and analysis confirming the breach, attempted credential revocation via IAM/PAM controls was denied due to policy and evidence linkage issues. The incident remains unresolved from an active mitigation standpoint, requiring urgent procedural and technical review.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 initiated a port scan (ET SCAN Nmap SYN Scan) against internal host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101). Alert logged with low severity.
Successful authentication from 10.0.2.15 to domain controller (10.0.1.1) using CORP\helpdesk account.
SIEM correlation identifies 23 successful lateral movements and authentication events tied to Finance OU accounts. Pass-the-hash attack confirmed.
Automated response attempted bulk credential revocation for 23 compromised Finance accounts via IAM/PAM system. Action denied due to lack of policy approval and insufficient evidence linkage.

arguments.summary: A critical credential compromise incident was detected in the Finance OU. The external IP 185.220.101.42 conducted reconnaissance via port scanning on 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101), followed by lateral movement and pass-the-hash attacks compromising all 23 accounts in the Finance department. Despite detection, automated credential revocation via IAM/PAM was denied due to policy constraints and lack of direct evidence linking individual logins to malicious activity. UEBA scored risk as low due to normal access patterns, indicating detection gaps in identifying lateral movement and credential misuse.

UEBA analysis returns low risk score (0.35) for user 'finance_user' due to normal behavioral patterns despite anomalous access volume.
SIEM correlation identifies 23 successful authentications originating from 10.0.10.51, all targeting Finance OU accounts.
Critical finding: All 23 Finance OU accounts compromised via pass-the-hash. Bulk credential revocation attempted via IAM/PAM tool (T8), but denied due to policy and evidence mismatch.

arguments.summary: APT-28 conducted a multi-stage compromise originating from external IP 45.33.32.156. Initial access was achieved via an unpatched public-facing system (WS-IT-101, 10.0.2.15), which was used as a pivot point to authenticate to the domain controller (10.0.1.1). The threat actor performed reconnaissance and successfully compromised Kerberos TGTs, leading to a critical severity incident. Immediate containment actions were authorized under BCP Alpha and PCI-DSS Requirement 8.1.4, but IAM and firewall controls failed to execute due to approval workflow bottlenecks. A cryptocurrency miner (Miner.CoinHive.A) was identified and removed from the initial host.

timeline.description: External IP 45.33.32.156 conducted Nmap SYN scan against WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Detected and logged by IDS.
Successful authentication from WS-IT-101 to domain controller (10.0.1.1) as CORP\helpdesk. Likely credential reuse or compromise.
Suspicious PowerShell activity detected on WS-IT-101 (correlated via SIEM). Potential privilege escalation and Kerberos TGT request.
BCP Protocol Alpha invoked due to confirmed Kerberos TGT compromise. Immediate account revocation required.
